meaning_en: Lasting for a very short time
example: Fame on social media is often ephemeral.
mnemonic: Ephemeral sounds like 'a funeral'—life and moments pass quickly.

example: The benevolent donor funded a new village school.
mnemonic: Bene- means 'good' (like benefit), and volent means 'wishing'—wishing good for others.

meaning_en: Stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or course of action
example: Despite clear evidence, he remained obdurate.
mnemonic: Obdurate sounds like 'hard door'—a door that will not budge.

meaning_en: Having or showing keen mental discernment and good judgment
example: Her sagacious advice saved the team from a costly mistake.
mnemonic: A sage is a wise person, so sagacious means full of sage-like wisdom.

meaning_en: Having or showing care and conscientiousness in one's work or duties
example: Diligent aspirants revise daily for SSC exams.
mnemonic: Diligent is 'daily-gent'—someone who works daily with gentle focus.

meaning_en: To face a difficult or unpleasant situation with courage
meaning_hi: कठिन परिस्थिति का साहसपूर्वक सामना करना
example: She decided to bite the bullet and take the tough mock test.
mnemonic: Soldiers in the past bit on a lead bullet during painful surgery without anesthesia.

example: He visits his hometown once in a blue moon.
mnemonic: A second full moon in a calendar month (a blue moon) is an uncommon event.

meaning_en: To work or study late into the night
meaning_hi: देर रात तक मेहनत या पढ़ाई करना
example: Many candidates burn the midnight oil before the exam.
mnemonic: Before electric lamps, people burned oil lamps late at night to keep working.

meaning_en: To reveal a secret unintentionally or prematurely
meaning_hi: राज़ खोल देना या भेद उजागर करना
example: He accidentally spilled the beans about the surprise party.
mnemonic: Picture knocking over a jar of beans so the secret spills out everywhere.

meaning_en: To stop working on something for the day
meaning_hi: आज के लिए काम बंद करना
example: After six hours of practice, we decided to call it a day.
mnemonic: You officially declare the workday finished and pack up.

meaning_en: A person who disinterestedly and selflessly is concerned for the well-being of others
example: The altruist donated his entire pension to charity.
mnemonic: Altruist sounds like 'all-true-ist'—truly caring for all others.

meaning_hi: सर्वज्ञानी या सब कुछ जानने वाला
example: An omniscient narrator knows every character's thoughts.
mnemonic: Omni- means 'all' and sci- means 'know' (like science)—knowing all.

example: That dance trend proved to be an ephemeral craze.
mnemonic: Think of a mayfly living for just one day—here today, gone tomorrow.

meaning_en: A person knowing and using several languages
example: As a polyglot, she speaks five languages fluently.

meaning_en: A person who tends to see the worst aspect of things or believe that the worst will happen
example: A pessimist expects rain even on a sunny morning.
mnemonic: Pessimist rhymes with 'mess-in-mist'—always expecting a gloomy mess.
